[[Zamalek SC]] | continentalcup2 = [[2012 CAF Confederation Cup]] | continentalcup2 qualifiers = [[ENPPI Club|ENPPI]] (cup winner) | league topscorer = [[Ahmed Abd El-Zaher]] [[Shikabala]] (13 goals) | biggest home win = [[Ismaily]] 5–0 [[El-Entag El-Harby]] | biggest away win = [[Wadi Degla Sporting Club|Wadi Degla]] 0–5 [[Haras El Hodood]] | highest scoring = [[Union Alexandria|El-Ittihad]] 3–6 [[El-Entag El-Harby]] | matches = 240 | total goals = 571 | longest wins = | longest unbeaten = | longest losses = | highest attendance = | lowest attendance = | average attendance = 6,732 | prevseason = [[2009–10 Egyptian Premier League|2009–10]] | nextseason = [[2011–12 Egyptian Premier League|2011–12]]}} The '''2010–11 Egyptian Premier League''' was the fifty-fourth season of the [[Egyptian Premier League]] since its establishment in 1948. It began on 5 August 2010 and ended on 11 July 2011.[https://web.archive.org/web/20110625023557/http://www.fifa.com/associations/association=egy/nationalleague/date=072011.html Egyptian league's fixtures and results] The league was suspended on 27 January 2011 due to the [[2011 Egyptian Revolution|Egyptian Revolution]] and resumed on 13 April 2011.[https://web.archive.org/web/20110506025430/http://www.fifa.com/associations/association=egy/nationalleague/date=042011.html Egyptian league's fixtures and results] A total of 16 teams are contesting the league including six-time defending champions [[Al-Ahly S.C.]] who have won thirty-five times in total. == Teams == [[Ghazl El-Mehalla]], [[El Mansoura SC]] and [[Asyut Petroleum]] as the worst three teams of the [[2009–10 Egyptian Premier League|2009–10]] were relegated to the [[2010–11 Egyptian Second Division]].
